## VHDL Example

```{vhdl}
type state is (S0, S1, S2);
signal c_st, n_st : state;

p_seq: process (rst, clk)                       -- <1>
begin
  if rst = '1' then
    c_st <= S0;
  elsif rising_edge(clk) then
    c_st <= n_st;
  end if;
end process;

p_com: process (i, c_st)                        -- <2>
begin
  -- default assignments                        -- <2>
  n_st <= c_st; -- remain in current state      -- <2>
  o <= '1'; -- most frequent value              -- <2>
  -- specific assignments                       -- <2>
  case c_st is                                  -- <2>
    when S0 =>                                  -- <2>
      if i = "00" then                        -- <2>
        n_st <= S1;                             -- <2>
      end if;                                   -- <2>
  end case;
end process;
```

## C++ Example

```{cpp}
#include <iostream>

int main() {                                   // <1>
  std::cout << "Hello, world!" << std::endl; // <1>
  return 0;                                   // <1>
}

void foo(int x) {                              // <2>
```

2. Function example.
1.explanation:
1. Save the snippet above as `test-annotations.qmd` in an otherwise empty directory.
2. Run `quarto render test-annotations.qmd --to html` (or simply `quarto preview`).
3. Inspect the rendered HTML: you will see the numbered annotation list at the bottom (① Initialize sequential logic, ② Describe combinatorial logic, etc.) but the inline markers `-- <1>` / `// <2>` remain visible in the code block rather than being replaced by circled numbers in the code gutter or hidden entirely.

This reproduces the bug in Quarto 1.3.302 where annotations in C/C++ and VHDL blocks are detected but not applied to the code rendering in the same way as R, Python, or other languages.
1.bug_scenario: When you include a VHDL or C/C++ code block in a Quarto document with inline annotation markers (e.g. `-- <1>` or `// <2>`) and you set `code-annotations: below` (or `true`), Quarto detects the annotation markers and generates the footnote list correctly, but it fails to replace or hide the inline markers in the code itself. Instead of seeing circled numbers in the gutter (or the markers entirely removed from the code), you still see the raw `<1>`,`<2>` markers in your rendered HTML.
